headline: Chinese-speaking phishing takedown, state AI attack tooling, and the Jensen Huang spy saga
overview: Today's shows cover a coordinated civil and infrastructure takedown of a Chinese-speaking phishing ecosystem, reports of state groups and criminals adopting agentic AI attack frameworks, and a long analysis of the alleged espionage story around Nvidia's chief executive. Several shows also touch on AI's effect on the criminal marketplace and on the business side of the AI boom.

topStories.title: Takedown of Chinese-speaking phishing ecosystem
topStories.summary: A Microsoft-led civil action and infrastructure takedown targeted the Kogui and related fishing kit families and the wider marketplace enablers, which were responsible for very high volumes of phishing, many aimed at Japanese users.

topStories.title: State actors and criminals adopt agentic AI attack tools
topStories.summary: Microsoft reports Chinese and North Korean state groups integrating the Artex framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation. Swiss and Italian agencies warn of autonomous AI attack agents targeting critical infrastructure.

topStories.title: Alleged espionage story around Nvidia's chief executive
topStories.summary: A former intelligence officer discusses the alleged use of a romantic relationship and business access to cultivate a technology executive, and the policy and security questions the case raises ahead of congressional hearings.

topStories.title: Data breaches at travel and password companies
topStories.summary: Flight Centre disclosed a breach exposing some passport details and other customer records, and 1Password reported an attacker accessing a corporate GitHub account.

topStories.title: Anthropic's rise to a major AI company
topStories.summary: A history episode traces how Anthropic's shift toward coding and agentic products drove rapid revenue growth and changed how the AI business model works.

episodes.title: Taking the bait out of phishing.
episodes.summary: A rebroadcast of an earlier episode, presented as a holiday encore. It covers a Microsoft-led civil lawsuit and takedown against the Chinese-speaking fishing kit ecosystem, including the Kogui family and related marketplace enablers, which Microsoft says enabled over a billion malicious messages.

episodes.title: ARTEX framework thrives, autonomous cyberattack warning, Australian travel agent breach
episodes.summary: Covers Chinese and North Korean state groups adding the AI-driven Artex offensive framework to their toolkits, a Swiss and Italian warning about autonomous AI attack agents, a Flight Center breach exposing customer passport details, a UK Home Office GDPR reprimand over wrongly detained people, and Palo Alto Networks warning of exploitation of a chained PHP and Fragnesia flaw.

episodes.title: Jensen Huang Scandal - A Former Security Operative's View
episodes.summary: A special edition with former intelligence officer Neil Bisson on the alleged spy story involving Nvidia's chief executive and a woman linked to the Chinese Ministry of State Security. They discuss how such approaches are built slowly over time, the security implications for technology executives, and upcoming congressional hearings.

episodes.title: How Anthropic Went From Anti-Product to $81B a Year
episodes.summary: Holiday replacement episode sharing excerpts from a longer history show on how Anthropic grew from a safety-focused research lab into a major revenue-generating AI company, driven by coding models and agentic products.

episodes.title: He brought bitcoin mining to his hometown. Then came the noise.
episodes.summary: Revisits a story about a man who brought Bitcoin mining to his grandfather's hometown in Kentucky after state incentives, and the local noise problems that followed. The notes do not cover further specifics.

episodes.title: Cyber Bites - 27th November 2026
episodes.summary: Short news roundup covering a bank penalty over a 2023 cyber incident, a 1Password breach involving a corporate GitHub account, and the Flight Centre customer data breach.

episodes.title: AI Arms Race, We All Lose - PSW #954
episodes.summary: Covers a range of topics including AI accelerating exploit writing, AI-driven reverse engineering, shrinking disclosure timelines, malware A/B testing, and exposed fridge controllers. The notes are a topic list, so detail on each item is limited.
